text: VN-Index falls for four days in a row
HÀ NỘI - Indices closed marginally lower on Friday as buying interest returned in the afternoon session, helping the VN-Index recover most of its earlier losses despite widespread selling pressure.
On the Hochiminh Stock Exchange (HoSE), the VN-Index shed 0.83 points to close at 1,688.79 points.
The market breadth remained negative, with 217 stocks declining against 96 gainers.
The VN30 basket showed a more balanced performance, with 13 stocks advancing, 13 falling and four ending unchanged.
Liquidity improved from the previous session, increasing to over VNĐ15.96 trillion (US$617 million).
The HNX-Index on the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) also fell 4.35 points to 234.59 points.
Buying demand picked up during the afternoon, allowing the VN-Index to reverse its earlier decline and approach the reference level before ending the session slightly in negative territory.
Vietcombank (VCB), MBBank (MBB), VPBank (VPB) and BIDV (BID) were the biggest drags, collectively taking more than 3.56 points off the VN-Index.
By contrast, VIC of Vingroup, Techcombank (TCB), Sacombank (STB) and PV Gas (GAS) contributed a combined 5.33 points, helping the benchmark recover much of its intraday losses.
The HNX-Index performed less favourably, coming under pressure from several declining stocks.

Thaiholdings JSC (HD) hit the floor prices for the second day, while National Citizen Commercial Joint Stock Bank (NVB) fell 2.01 per cent, Sunshine Group (KSF) lost 0.74 per cent and Vinacomin - Power Holding Corporation (DTK) declined 4.85 per cent.
Foreign investors remained net sellers on HoSE, offloading nearly VNĐ841 billion.
FPT shares of FPT Corporation faced the strongest selling pressure, with foreign net sales of approximately VNĐ157 billion.

Saigon - Hanoi Securities said the market continued to weaken under pressure from global markets and increased net selling by foreign investors, with selling pressure intensifying across several sectors.
The securities firm noted that market quality and capital flows had yet to improve.
OCBS Securities expected that the VN-Index would likely continue fluctuating within the 1,680-1,700-point range.
It advised investors to remain patient and avoid panic selling, noting that the market's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio had fallen to a low level.
Analysts also pointed to opportunities among companies that continued to deliver strong earnings growth while trading at valuations below the market average.
Stocks meeting emerging-market criteria were also expected to attract capital from investment funds.
Nevertheless, analysts recommended that investors prioritise companies with sound fundamentals and prepare to deploy capital once the market confirms a stable trading range. - BIZHUB/VNS
